requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled, permanent rules were installed, node1 was restarted with a changed boot identity, and the firewall, runtime rules, SSH, and expected traffic behavior recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The active zone retained the unrestricted SSH service; both node2 and node3 received SSH banners before and after node1's restart, and final observation showed SSH active on IPv4 and IPv6 listeners.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 on node1 only from node2.
requirements.summary: With a bounded listener running on node1, node2 received HTTP 200 before and after node1's restart and again after node2's restart. Final compiled rules contained the source-specific acceptance for node2's address ahead of the catch-all rejects.

requirements.requirement: Reject TCP port 9000 from node3 and every other source.
requirements.summary: Node3's connection was rejected both before and after restarts while node2 could reach the same live listener. Final runtime, permanent, and compiled rules showed catch-all TCP/9000 rejects for remaining IPv4 and IPv6 traffic.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained RHEL 10.0 on kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The existing platform firewalld service was used, and package-health observations remained clean.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent firewalld policy that keeps SSH open, admits TCP/9000 from node2's managed address, and rejects other IPv4 and IPv6 sources. Behavior and persistence were demonstrated across node restarts, while the OS and kernel remained unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on all three nodes and agrees with the fixed boot-identity observations.
limitations: Live TCP/9000 behavior was exercised from node2 and node3, not from an additional arbitrary IPv4 source or an IPv6 source; coverage of all other sources is established by direct inspection of the compiled catch-all reject rules.

The fixed lifecycle collector provides generic platform and health observations rather than an independent firewall-policy probe; task-specific firewall behavior is evidenced by the executor command outputs.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent firewall changes were required by the contract. Temporary TCP/9000 listeners and files were bounded verification prerequisites and were removed; final evidence and the lifecycle snapshot show no port-9000 listener or test-file residue. Restarts of all three nodes were required by the provider-wide evidence protocol, and each had a pre-restart healthy state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered relevant services and behavior. No failed services, damaged package state, or unrelated exposure was observed.
